title: O(1) Budget Guard with Refunds and a Rescan Oracle
instructions: In `budget/guard.py` implement `BudgetGuard` (per-tenant running counters; `charge`, `refund`, `used`), with the declared exceptions `BudgetExceededError(tenant, limit)` and `UnknownCallError`, and the slow oracle `RescanGuard` that recomputes usage from the full call history. `charge` must validate every limit before changing anything, be atomic under threads, and never depend on how many calls were made before.

evidence.label: charge adds to usage and refund reverses exactly that call
Each charge returns a new call id
A rejected charge changes no limit, not even the ones that would have fit
Using exactly the cap is allowed, one more unit is not
Negative amounts and unknown limit names raise ValueError and change nothing
Refunding an unknown or already refunded call raises UnknownCallError
The guard matches the RescanGuard oracle on seeded random charges and refunds
400 concurrent one-token charges against a cap of 200 succeed exactly 200 times
